title: Golarion grounding: our own 1950s alternate-history branch
summary: The campaign is explicitly set on Golarion, in a different (1950s retrofuturistic, Giant Robo-styled) era, using light specific real-Golarion touches — Pharasma temples, real ancestry terms, real location names — rather than either a fully homebrew setting or a straight Golarion campaign.
description:
Clarifying statement of setting identity: this is Golarion (Pathfinder/Starfinder's default campaign world), just a different era from the one usually depicted — 'our own 1950's style Golarion with a retrofuturistic Giant Robo styled world.' The intent is to sprinkle in real, specific Golarion lore where it serves the story rather than either ignoring Golarion entirely or trying to run a fully faithful Golarion campaign: examples given include mentioning temples of Pharasma (goddess of death and fate — thematically apt given the campaign's mortality/endurance themes), using proper ancestry terminology, and referencing real Golarion locations by their actual names. Explicit framing: 'we can make the adventure true to bits of Golarion that work for what we're doing' — cherry-pick, don't feel bound.

Giant Robo is named directly as a tonal reference — a specific, deliberate genre touchstone distinct from (and additional to) the earlier-established decision that this campaign is not copying Evangelion's plot.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — large worldbuilding/tooling brain-dump.
openSubQuestions: Which specific real Golarion locations/deities/lore beyond Pharasma are worth referencing — not enumerated yet. (In use since: Kortos, Absalom and a temple of Pharasma, LEDGER #25 and #28.)

How this interacts with the naming placeholders that are still open (now kept in data/campaign/open-questions.json) — some could plausibly resolve toward real-Golarion-adjacent names, but not decided. The city (Kurose) and the Directorate (特別対策本部) have since been named, both in Japanese.
